front-nine.notes:
FRONT-NINE RESEARCH SUMMARY (Westmount G&CC, Kitchener ON). Research used text only: WebSearch, WebFetch and small curl probes. No browser was used and no media was played. Probe files are saved under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-owner--sessions-cse-01KdqpZtNCdQ9mEvqKNRp2cj-Faire-ai-executor/465097aa-0f5b-58d7-b78f-3bbccea3f493/scratchpad/research_probe/.

MAIN SOURCE: a hole-by-hole ranking of all 18 holes by gcabbott, who joined Westmount as a member in 2018 (blog post dated 23 May 2020, written from the club's 2018 flyovers): https://gcabbott.wordpress.com/2020/05/23/ranking-the-18-holes-at-westmount-golf-and-country-club/. It is the only source that describes every front-nine hole. Supporting sources:
- top100golfcourses.com reviews by Dave Finn (19205), Eric Robinson (37889), Vinny Lazzara (41840, Jan 2025) and Matt Bosela (26855).
- SCOREGolf 2024-25 Canada Top 100 text, as republished by FOGOLF. Westmount was #13.
- UPI's 1990 du Maurier Classic preview.
- Golf Canada's coverage of the 2022 Canadian Women's Amateur, held at Westmount.

CLUB FLYOVERS: westmountgolf.com/theclub/golfcourseoverview.aspx embeds one Vimeo flyover per hole (2018). The pages carry no hole text. Vimeo IDs:
- H1 268453958, H2 268477865, H3 268477914, H4 268477951, H5 271303615, H6 268478009, H7 268478015, H8 268478018, H9 268478060.
- oEmbed confirms the titles 'Westmount G&CC Flyover Hole #N' (uploaded 2018-05-07, empty descriptions) for holes 1-4 and 6. The other four return 404 from oEmbed.
- The flyovers are the best visual reference for hand checks, but they were not watched.

SCORECARD:
- Front-nine pars are 5-4-3-4-5-3-5-4-4 (out 37); the course is par 73. Both scorecards agree on the pars.
- GolfPass blue yardages for holes 1-9: 559/373/195/412/558/202/541/283/401, out 3524. GolfPass lists the course total as 6943 but its holes add up to 6925.
- AllSquare blue yardages (last edited July 2020): 559/368/200/416/562/200/540/289/400.
- Men's stroke index for holes 1-9 (AllSquare): 3/11/17/7/1/15/5/13/9.
- Golf Canada lists 7,018 yds, so a newer back tee probably exists.

HISTORY THAT AFFECTS THE ROUTING:
- top100golfcourses.com: Thompson's 1931 layout was par 71. Land added in 1958 brought in three new holes, and Thompson's opening three holes became the practice facility.
- gcabbott: today's holes 5-7 are the Robbie Robinson holes, and today's 3rd was Thompson's original 6th.
- Doug Carrick reshaped every bunker and rebuilt the 11th and 12th greens (ASGCA; top100 dates it 2015). WAC Golf, whose Keith Cutten managed the job for the contractor, places the work around 2013.
- Bunker descriptions written before that renovation may be out of date. Finn's review mentions the 2015 clubhouse work, so it is post-2015.

ROUTING CLUES FOR MATCHING OSM AND LiDAR:
- The 3rd tee is next to the clubhouse patio.
- The 4th green sits at a central hub with the Oasis snack shop and on-course washrooms; the washrooms double as a weather shelter (club visitors page).
- The club also lists weather shelters at the pump house behind the reservoir and behind the 14th green.
- Finn: the walks to the 5th and 8th tees are confusing for non-members, which suggests longer green-to-tee transitions.
- Bosela: the par 5s are front-loaded (holes 1, 5 and 7). Many tee shots play downhill, and many holes climb gently from the landing area to the green.
- General character (top100golfcourses.com): fairways 'dipping and rising, seldom allowing the golfer a level lie'; wide landing areas; 'flashed bunkers prevail around the greens'. The club calls an uneven stance a 'Westmount lie'.

NOT FOUND:
- No club-written hole descriptions or yardage-book text.
- No golfclubatlas.com thread or Ian Andrew blog post specific to Westmount turned up.
- No source gives the dogleg direction for holes 1, 2, 4, 8 or 9 (hole 4 is only called 'angled'), or bunker counts beyond hole 2 (one, right) and hole 8 (three).
- No creek is mentioned on any front-nine hole. The only front-nine water is the decorative pond with fountain on hole 3.

lidar-sources.recommendation:
Use OMAFRA Lidar 2016-18, Lake Erie package (NRCan project Lake_Erie_2018). It is the only public classified point cloud covering the whole course, and it is also the newest one that does.

The newer Upper Thames-Grand River 2025 project leaves a hole over central Kitchener-Waterloo. Its nearest tiles to the course are at N4816-4817.

The course needs six 1 km COPC tiles, all with HTTP 200 confirmed, plus HTTP 206 on range requests:
- 1km175360481002018LLAKEERIE
- 1km175360481102018LLAKEERIE
- 1km175370481002018LLAKEERIE
- 1km175370481102018LLAKEERIE
- 1km175380481002018LLAKEERIE
- 1km175380481102018LLAKEERIE

They are at https://canelevation-lidar-point-clouds.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/pointclouds_nuagespoints/ON/Lake_Erie_2018/<tile>.copc.laz.

Key facts:
- **Acquisition:** leaf-off, 2018-03-21 and 2018-03-25, plus one 2017-12-06 line. Leica ALS70-HP.
- **Density:** 8 pts/m² nominal. Measured 14-20 pts/m² counting all returns, 10-15 counting first returns.
- **Classes seen:** 1, 2, 6, 7, 17 and 18. No class 9 was sampled.
- **CRS:** NAD83(CSRS) UTM 17N, EPSG:2958.
- **Heights:** CGVD2013 (EPSG:6647), but each file's WKT says VERT_CS "unknown", so assign 2958+6647 explicitly.

The course bbox in EPSG:2958 is E 536893-538161, N 4810400-4811319, which is about 500 m south of the brief's estimate.

Rather than downloading all 591 MB, use readers.copc in PDAL or laspy CopcReader with bounds of about [536850-538200, 4810350-4811370]. Filter classes 7 and 18; tile 538/4810 is noisy. Build the DTM from class 2 points at 0.25-0.5 m.

Licence: OGL-Ontario / OGL-Canada. Redistributing the derived GSPro terrain is allowed with the attribution 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Ontario'.

Fallbacks:
- NRCan HRDEM 1 m DTM/DSM COGs built from the same 2018 data (EPSG:3979).
- City of Kitchener 2019 1 m DTM/DSM. It is leaf-on and only covers part of the course: the north-west part lies in the City of Waterloo and has no data.

Check the 2018 surface against current imagery for any renovated tees, greens or bunkers.

scorecard-aggregators.card_date: No card I could fetch gives an effective date. The newest is the Golf Ontario (GAO) BlueGolf card (Blue 6943, 73.0/130, with White/Blue, Red/White and Gold/Red combos), shown on the site in 2026. Reasons it is newest: (1) It is the provincial golf association's own course record, and its ratings are newer than GolfPass's 72.4/133-era values, which Where2Golf also still uses. (2) It is the only card that adds up and hangs together: the hole yardages sum exactly to every printed total, and every combo hole equals one of its two parent tees. (3) Hole19 independently stores the same Blue yardages, in metres, along with ratings close to GAO's (72.9/130, 71.1/126). Golfify and AllSquare carry the same ratings and combo tees. (4) The old GolfPass hole data has Blue H11 at 556; GAO has 568. That fits the 11th green being rebuilt in Carrick's master-plan work (ASGCA, Nov 2013: work had begun; Top100: bunkers and greens 11 and 12 done in 2015; Carrick: completion scheduled for 2016). This last point is my inference, not a dated fact. The GAO card therefore most likely dates from after the 2015–16 work and after the WHS-era re-rating (2020 or later), but I could not confirm the exact year.

facts.statement: Only one water hazard is mapped in OSM inside the course: way 918946248 (golf=water_hazard, natural=water). It is a small pond of about 890 m2 (about 47 m E-W by 35 m N-S), centroid 43.44961 N, -80.53636 W, on the par-3 3rd hole about 100 m west of the clubhouse. In the 2025 Esri aerial it is a dark, tree-shaded pond lying roughly 60 m from the 3rd tee and about 10-15 m right (north-east) of the tee-to-green line. It is the only water close to the line of play.

A second, larger pond is in the woods in the south-west part of the course: OSM way 148323977 (natural=water), about 3,900 m2 (about 62 x 90 m), centroid 43.44759 N, -80.54169 W, roughly 60 m from the centrelines of holes 6, 7 and 5. The aerial shows an engineered pond with a bare earth or gravel rim and a small structure on its east bank (approx 43.4477, -80.5412). The club's visitor page mentions shelters 'at the pump house behind the reservoir', so this pond is very likely the irrigation reservoir and pump house (that identification is an inference). It is mostly out of play.

Maple Hills Creek (OSM waterway=stream, imported from CanVec in 2009, ways 199916191, 824691391/824691392 (culvert, layer -1), 199916190, 39968224) runs north along the west edge of the course. It sits about 5-15 m outside the OSM course boundary, between the course and University Avenue West, about 50 m west of the 7th hole centreline. It passes through a culvert near 43.4524, -80.5422 by the apparent maintenance yard and continues north-east outside the course behind Lourdes St / Somerset Cres. An unnamed CanVec stream (way 199916205) lies further west, beyond University Ave. No source describes a creek in play on any hole. CanVec positions are only approximate.

Thompson routed the course 'through bush and swampland'. In 1997 superintendent Hugh Kirkpatrick said 'We preserve wetlands', and that Westmount was among the first Canadian courses to join the Audubon Cooperative Sanctuary System.

The club was formed in 1929 (board first met 17 June 1929; Wikipedia gives the founding as 7 Sept 1929) by members of Grand River G&CC. Stanley Thompson designed the course and supervised its construction, which began in 1929 and cost $49,679.73. The original layout was 6,440 yd, par 71, and it opened to members in 1931. The site is about 160 acres, and the grounds cross the Kitchener/Waterloo municipal boundary.

In 1958 extra land was acquired and the course went from par 71 to par 73. Three new holes were added 'at the expense of the opening trio, which were turned into a practice facility'. That practice ground is the east lobe of the property, where the driving range now is.

Architects credited by aggregator sites: Stanley Thompson (1931), C.E. 'Robbie' Robinson (1961), Thomas McBroom (1986 and 1997), Doug Carrick and Ian Andrew (listed as 2015). The Ian Andrew credit and the 2015 date have no primary source (see the next fact for the dated primary sources).

Carrick Design has advised Westmount since 2003. Carrick reshaped all the bunkers and redesigned the 11th and 12th greens to restore a Stanley Thompson character. The work was completed in fall 2013 (ASGCA, 8 Apr 2014: 'completed last fall'), with Keith Cutten as the contractor's project manager in 2013. Top100golfcourses and other aggregators date the same bunker and 11/12-green work to 2015, which is probably wrong.

Work up to 1997 under superintendent Hugh Kirkpatrick (superintendent from 1979): most tees redone, going from 2 tee sets to 4; four greens rebuilt to USGA specification; practice range redone with 10 target greens. He said bunker restoration ('copy [Thompson's] style'; 'You don't see his bunkers here') was planned for 1998, along with replacing the then 25-year-old irrigation system (installed c.1972). The McBroom 1997 credit probably refers to this period. No source found for a post-2000 irrigation replacement.

Club timeline since 2000: in 2015 a major clubhouse renovation (spike room, founders room, entrance), reported at about $2.6M and including a new patio; in 2017 the halfway house (originally built 1968) was renovated and pickleball added; in 1999 the tennis courts were converted to Har-Tru clay. No public record found of tree-removal programs or new irrigation after 2000.

Scorecard: par 73, split 37 out and 36 in (UPI, 1990 du Maurier Classic, when the course measured 6,415 yd; the 5th was a 544-yd par 5). Current tees: Blue 6,943 yd (72.4/133), White 6,565 (70.6/126), Red 6,125 (68.9/118), Gold 5,472 (66.0/111). Golf Canada lists a total of 7,018 yd. Course record 64, set by George Bayer at the 1957 Canadian Open.

OSM golf=hole pars by hole: 5,4,3,4,5,3,5,4,4 (front 37) and 4,5,3,5,4,4,4,3,4 (back 36). This matches par 37-36-73 and the reviewers' notes (#3 par 3, #5 par 5, #7 long par 5, #12 short par 3, #14 par 4). OSM also maps 58 tees, 48 bunkers, 18 greens and 17 fairways. Approximate tee-to-green bearings: 1:342, 2:173, 3:307, 4:296, 5:158, 6:268, 7:359, 8:66, 9:159, 10:114, 11:267, 12:329, 13:334, 14:152, 15:91, 16:298, 17:337, 18:128 degrees.

Holes near the clubhouse (OSM way 69020082, centroid 43.44903, -80.53518). Distances are from that centroid: 3rd tee about 45 m W; 18th green about 55 m WSW; 10th tee about 75 m SSE; 9th green about 100 m NW; 1st tee about 125 m E (towards the tennis courts and range); 2nd green and 4th tee about 135-145 m N/NW. The 1st runs north up the east side of the property, and the 10th heads east to the south-east corner. All 18 holes sit on one contiguous parcel; no public road or trail crosses the course. Inverness Drive (reached via Glasgow St and Aberdeen Rd from Fischer-Hallman) is the dead-end entrance road to the clubhouse.

The club's visitor page places on-course features as follows: weather shelters at the pump house behind the reservoir, behind the 14th green, and at the on-course washrooms at the #4 green; clocks are installed around the course. Per where2golf, the par-4 14th's 'narrowing fairway drops down to a well-bunkered green' backed by tall mature trees. Per a 2025 review, the par-3 12th plays 'from an elevated platform to an elevated green'.

Residential lots surround the course on every side; there is no Westmount Rd or Highland Rd frontage. Adjacent roads: University Avenue West, a curving arterial along the whole west side (about 13-28 m from the boundary, about 73 m from the hole 7 centreline); Glasgow Street on the south-east edge (about 40 m from the hole 11 centreline); and the residential streets Maple Hill Dr, Knell Dr and Briar Patch Ln (south), Inverness Dr, Huntley Cres, Aberdeen Rd and Westgate Walk (east, around the range), McDonald Pl, Stanley Dr and Forsyth Dr (north-east), and Somerset Cres and Lourdes St (north).

Holes most exposed to the boundary or houses, by OSM centreline distance to the boundary and number of buildings within 60 m: 12 (18 m; 2 houses, Maple Hill Dr), 1 (23 m; 6, McDonald Pl/Stanley Dr), 8 (27 m; 8, Lourdes St/Somerset Cres), 10 (27 m; 4, Inverness/Huntley/Westgate), 11 (34 m; 2, Glasgow St), 7 (38 m; University Ave W), 6 (42 m; 1), 9 (3 houses, Somerset Cres). Holes 3, 14, 16, 17 and 18 are interior, more than 120 m from the boundary. No public OB-stake map was found, so treat the property line (OSM 39971102, or the City of Kitchener golf-course polygon) as the OB line.

The City of Kitchener publishes a 'Golf_Course' open-data polygon layer of the course boundaries (NAD83 UTM 17N, EPSG:26917, stated accuracy +/-1 m, static). Its outline would be a good OB line. The Esri World Imagery tile over the course is Vantor/Maxar WorldView-2, dated 2025-06-02, 0.5 m resolution, with stated accuracy of 8.47 m, so it needs registering to LiDAR or OSM.

Greens are bentgrass and fairways poa annua (from aggregator listings). In 1997 the greens were described as bentgrass on 'a tremendously shaded golf course', with greenside fans installed to keep them alive (among the first this far north), and as 'small, old greens'.

No published stimpmeter figure was found. Descriptions: 'The greens are fast and slick' (UPI, 1990 LPGA week); 'greens are fast' (2023 review); approach shots face 'flashed bunkers' around 'dramatic and demanding' greens; fairways rarely give a level lie (the 'Westmount lie'). Tournament prep in 1997 meant double-cutting for speed. A sim value around 11-12 ft would be an assumption, not a sourced number.
Bunkers are flashed-face, Thompson-style, all reshaped by Carrick in 2013. In the June 2025 aerial the sand is bright white to light cream. The sand brand or type is not published.

The course is heavily tree-lined parkland: 'almost every fairway framed by towering maples and pines' (2020); 'Every hole is framed by large well maintained trees' (2025); 'elegantly tree-lined fairways' (where2golf); 'tremendously shaded' (1997). Since at least the 1990s the club has run woodlot management with a consulting arborist and its own tree nursery, removing dead or dying trees and transplanting 3-4 inch caliper nursery trees. The only species named in any source are maples and pines.

From the June 2025 aerial: canopy is mostly broadleaf deciduous (consistent with maple), with scattered darker conifers. Wide blocks of woods separate most parallel fairways, especially in the west and centre (holes 4-9 and 13-17); the densest belt is along University Ave W on the west. OSM maps about 19 natural=wood polygons in and around the course but has no species or leaf_type tags. Species split beyond maples and pines is unverified.

Main clubhouse: OSM way 69020082 'Westmount Golf Club', a footprint of about 3,330 m2 (about 63 x 105 m) at 43.44903, -80.53518, near the middle of the property. In the 2025 aerial the complex has dark brown / reddish-brown pitched shingle roofs plus a large flat grey roof block on its west side; that block is possibly the six-sheet curling rink built 1962-63 (unconfirmed). A second brown-roofed building (OSM 1169230296, about 1,545 m2) stands north of the main parking lot, and a small building (OSM 1169230297, about 340 m2) is east toward the 1st tee. Parking lots lie east and south-east, with the bag drop in front of the Pro Shop. A new dining room, patio and games room were added in 1975, and there was a major renovation in 2015. Wall cladding material is not documented in any source found.

The grass driving range is in the east lobe of the property (about 43.4498-43.4510 N, -80.5330 to -80.5285 W), hitting west to east between houses on Huntley Cres/Westgate Walk (north) and Inverness Dr (south). The 2025 aerial shows about 15 small target bunkers and a large bunkered target green at the east end, plus practice tee strips and short-game/putting areas next to the tennis courts. Other facilities: putting, chipping and pitching greens, a bunker practice area, and a members-only Golf Training Centre. Four clay (Har-Tru) tennis courts sit at about 43.4497, -80.5329 (OSM pitches 1491988531-34), next to pickleball and a curling rink.

Cart paths are not mapped in OSM and no published description was found. In the 2025 aerial they are narrow (about 2-2.5 m), light tan/grey and uncurbed, looking like stone-dust/gravel or weathered asphalt; the surface is not confirmed. They run mainly beside tees and greens rather than continuously along fairways. Golf carts have GPS (GolfPass). A gravel/dirt compound at about 43.4520, -80.5418, reached by a service road off University Ave W, appears to be the maintenance yard (inference). The halfway house dates from 1968 (renovated 2017); there are on-course washrooms at the 4th green.

Searches for GSPro, TGC 2019, PGA Tour 2K21/2K23 and golf-simulator forum or Reddit listings found no existing simulator version of Westmount G&CC. A third-party list of GSPro Ontario courses (Cravin Sim Golf) does not include it. This is a negative result from text search only; the GSPro in-app course list could not be checked.

back-nine.notes:
BACK-NINE RESEARCH SUMMARY (sources fetched 2026-10-11; no browser tools used)

Scorecard (GolfPass, Blue/White/Red/Gold): 10 P4 334/319/304/217; 11 P5 556/531/492/448; 12 P3 141/127/108/93; 13 P5 554/520/503/439; 14 P4 375/359/318/293; 15 P4 453/396/367/315; 16 P4 439/418/400/359; 17 P3 165/149/132/113; 18 P4 384/367/351/334. Back nine par 36, course par 73 (37-36). Total yardage is 6943 on GolfPass and where2golf, and 7018 on Golf Canada. All Square Golf has a different, probably older scorecard (e.g. 10=310, 15=382, 16=401 in its Blue column, and its own text says 16 is 447). Its men's handicaps for 10-18 are 10, 2, 18, 4, 14, 6, 8, 16, 12, which differ from GolfPass. Use the GolfPass yardages and check them against LiDAR and OSM hole lengths.

Club website: the official course tour (westmountgolf.com/theclub/golfcourseoverview.aspx, with pages golfcourseoverview_hole10 through _hole18) has hole thumbnails and Vimeo flyovers only, and no text. The flyover video IDs for holes 10-18 are 268478067, 268478071, 268478121, 268478125, 268478129, 268478159, 268478165, 268478172 and 268478176. Vimeo returns 404 or 'Sorry' for them (private or domain-locked), so their titles and descriptions cannot be read. The 'Course Map' image on the visitors page covers only the clubhouse, putting green, 1st tee and range. The visitors page says inclement-weather shelters are at 'the pump house behind the reservoir, behind the 14th green and the on-course washrooms at #4 green'.

Course-wide character from multiple sources, useful for terrain and green modelling:
- Top100: 'Fairways flow with the contours, dipping and rising, seldom allowing the golfer a level lie. Landing areas for tee shots are wide, but flashed bunkers prevail around the greens.'
- Matt Bosela (Top100, 2020): 'no forced carries', 'many appealing downhill tee shots', and 'many holes slowly climb from the landing area to the green'.
- Dave Finn (Top100, 2017): 'large greens are fast with subtle breaks', 'not as much dramatic elevation changes as I would have expected', 'open and groomed under the trees', and stones rise in the bunkers.
- 1990 LPGA preview (UPI): 'undulating fairways and greens', 'traps waiting to catch stray tee shots', 'greens are fast and slick'.
- Ian Andrew (2009): Westmount was built to 'a more modest bunker style' than Thompson's flamboyant courses. Carrick reshaped all bunkers in 2015.
- The course was 'routed through bush and swampland'. In 1958, three new holes were added 'at the expense of the opening trio', which became the practice facility. This presumably affects the front nine, but the sources do not say which holes.
- Green speed at the 2022 Canadian Women's Amateur was about 11 on the Stimpmeter (Turf & Rec).

Unverified or rejected claims: (1) A search-engine summary said a 'late 2022 routing change' added a new par-3 12th and a par-5 17th. No page I could read says this, and the June 2026 Golf Nomad review (par 3s at 12 and 17, last par 5 at 13) and the scorecard contradict it, so ignore it. (2) A search summary claimed the closing holes are called the 'Mad Mile' with a sign at the 15th tee. No source corroborates it, so I did not include it. No source mentions a creek or pond on any back-nine hole. The only water feature reviewers mention is the 'fountain pond' on the par-3 3rd (front nine). Locate any back-nine water from OSM and imagery.

Access notes: golfclubatlas.com returns a Cloudflare 403 to direct fetches, so two of its pages were read through Wayback Machine snapshots (URLs given above). The SCOREGolf course-guide page exists but blocks Anthropic's crawler, so it was not used. golfdigest.com and golfview.ca returned 403. Probe files are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-owner--sessions-cse-01KdqpZtNCdQ9mEvqKNRp2cj-Faire-ai-executor/465097aa-0f5b-58d7-b78f-3bbccea3f493/scratchpad/research_probe/.

sources.verified: HEAD gave 200 with Content-Length 16698320536, Accept-Ranges bytes, image/tiff. dem-imagery-sources.recommendation:
DEM (A): Use the NRCan HRDEM project COG ON-Lake_Erie_2018-1m from STAC collection 'hrdem-lidar' for the 5 km x 5 km backdrop:
https://canelevation-dem.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/hrdem-lidar/ON-Lake_Erie_2018-1m-dtm.tif
- Grid: 1 m, EPSG:3979, Float32, nodata -32767, heights in CGVD2013.
- Licence: OGL-Canada-2.0, so derived products can be redistributed with attribution.
- Coverage: it is the only remote COG that covers the whole square. I decoded tiles at all four corners and they were valid. The course centre reads 347.97 m.
- Use: gdalwarp it to EPSG:2958 (NAD83(CSRS) UTM 17N) over 534994,4808360 - 539994,4813360.

The hrdem-mosaic-1m item 8_2-mosaic-1m returns the same values here. Prefer the project file so the source is fixed.

For the course core, use the same 2018 lidar from LIO Elevation/Ontario_DTM_LidarDerived ImageServer:
- 0.5 m, native EPSG:2958, CGVD2013, OGL-Ontario.
- Course tiles: 1km1753{6,7,8}0481{0,1}02018LLAKEERIE.
- exportImage returned Float32 GeoTIFF; the centre pixel is 347.98 m.

Do not use these two:

sources.horizontal_crs: NAD83(CSRS) / UTM zone 17N, EPSG:2958. The WKT is COMPD_CS["NAD83(CSRS) / UTM zone 17N + unknown"] with PROJCS AUTHORITY EPSG 2958. NRCan states epoch 2010. sources.point_classes: Full-resolution and 1 m-resolution COPC queries over the course centre (200x200 m), the centre pond and the SW pond returned only classes 1 unclassified (includes vegetation), 2 ground, 6 building, 7 low noise and 18 high noise. There is no class 9 water anywhere on the course. The ponds return sparse points (about 4 pts/m² over the SW pond), most of them labelled class 2. The withheld, synthetic and overlap flags are all 0. Point source IDs at the centre are 8012 and 38012.
sources.resolution_or_density: The lift DBF gives a nominal 8 pts/m² (Leica ALS70-HP, 1000 m AGL, 500 kHz, 53 Hz scan, 40° FOV, 20% sidelap). sources.notes:
This is still the only public classified point cloud covering the course, and nothing newer covers it. I checked for a 2022-2024 OEMP block over Waterloo Region and found none:
- A group-by on the Ontario tile index over lon -81..-80, lat 43.1..43.8 lists GTA 2023, GTA 2014-18 (Halton/Milton/Peel), Hamilton-Niagara 2021, Huron-Georgian Bay 2022-23, Lake Erie 2016-18 and Upper Thames-Grand River 2025. At the course bbox the only project is Lake Erie.

- The imagery-derived point cloud index has only SWOOP 2015 at the course.

Processing cautions:
- Filter classes 7 and 18.
- Ponds have no class 9, so flatten water using OSM or imagery polygons.
- Leaf-off March data under-samples deciduous canopy, so use it for trunk positions and approximate heights, and take canopy extents from leaf-on imagery.
- Snow cover on the 2018-03-21/25 flights is not verified. Spot-check greens against the DTM if anything looks raised.

verify-sources.recommendation:
I re-tested every source that claims to cover the course on 2026-10-11 and every one of those claims holds. Nothing newer or denser than the 2018 lidar covers the course. I did find three things the researchers missed, listed at the end.

**Point cloud for the 0.25 m DEM and trees: OMAFRA Lidar 2016-18, Lake Erie package (NRCan project Lake_Erie_2018)**
- **Tiles:** six COPC tiles, all returning HTTP 200 and 206:
  - 1km175360481002018LLAKEERIE
  - 1km175360481102018LLAKEERIE
  - 1km175370481002018LLAKEERIE
  - 1km175370481102018LLAKEERIE
  - 1km175380481002018LLAKEERIE
  - 1km175380481102018LLAKEERIE
- **URL:** https://canelevation-lidar-point-clouds.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/pointclouds_nuagespoints/ON/Lake_Erie_2018/<tile>.copc.laz
- **Download:** about 591 MB in total. Stream only the course window instead, with PDAL readers.copc bounds ([536850,538200],[4810350,4811370]) in EPSG:2958.
- **Coordinates:** EPSG:2958. Assign the vertical datum as EPSG:6647 (CGVD2013); the file WKT says VERT_CS "unknown".
- **Heights:** class-2 points match the LIO CGVD2013 DTM to 0.01 m (347.98 vs 347.99 at one point, 347.15 vs 347.15 at another).
- **Flights:** leaf-off, 2018-03-21 and 2018-03-25, plus one line from 2017-12-06. Leica ALS70-HP.
- **Density:** 8 pts/m² nominal; the file headers average 14-20 pts/m² over all returns. On open turf there are about 11 ground points per m², which is roughly 0.7 per 0.25 m cell, so a 0.25 m DEM has to be interpolated (TIN or IDW). 0.5 m is the native-support resolution.
- **Classes:**
  - Drop classes 7 and 18.
  - There is no water class (9): the ponds return sparse class-2 points, so flatten them using OSM or imagery polygons.
  - Trees are class 1 above the ground. Because the flights were leaf-off, crowns are thin; place trunks and heights from the lidar and draw canopy outlines from leaf-on imagery.
- **Licence:** OGL-Ontario v1.0 / OGL-Canada 2.0. You can redistribute the GSPro terrain with the attribution "Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Ontario".

The newer Upper Thames-Grand River 2025 lidar leaves a hole over N4805-4816 in Kitchener-Waterloo, so it misses the course. No 2022-2024 Ontario block covers Waterloo Region.

**5 km DTM backdrop: NRCan HRDEM ON-Lake_Erie_2018-1m-dtm.tif**
- URL: https://canelevation-dem.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/hrdem-lidar/ON-Lake_Erie_2018-1m-dtm.tif
- It is a COG: 1 m, EPSG:3979, nodata -32767, CGVD2013, OGL-Canada-2.0.
- All four corners of the 5 km square read valid values.
- Warp it with gdalwarp /vsicurl/... -t_srs EPSG:2958 -te 534994 4808360 539994 4813360 -tr 1 1.
- The matching DSM COG (ON-Lake_Erie_2018-1m-dsm.tif) also works.

For the course core, use the LIO Ontario_DTM_LidarDerived ImageServer:
- It is 0.5 m, native EPSG:2958 and CGVD2013, built from the same lidar.
- Read it with exportImage F32, up to 30000 px per request.
- The Ontario_DSM_LidarDerived service is its 0.5 m DSM companion.

Do not mix in VILLE_WATERLOO 2014 (older, and missing the 5 km SE corner) or the Kitchener 2019 DTM. Kitchener's DTM is clipped at the Waterloo boundary, so it has no data over the course's north-west half. It also reads 0.4-0.6 m above the CGVD2013 sources, so it is probably CGVD28.

**Imagery for colour and tracing (reference only, not redistributable): Region of Waterloo ImageServers**
- **Imagery_2025:** 10 cm, June 23 - July 4, 2025, leaf-on. Use it for turf colour, mowing lines and canopy outlines.
- **Imagery_2026:** 10 cm, April 11-22, 2026, leaf-off. Use it for bunker, pond and cart-path edges under the trees.
- **Request:** https://gis.regionofwaterloo.ca/waimagery/rest/services/Imagery_2025/ImageServer/exportImage?bbox=...&bboxSR=26917&imageSR=26917&format=tiff&bandIds=0,1,2&f=image
- **Licence:** © First Base Solutions, with no open licence.
- **Alignment:** it is labelled EPSG:26917, but I measured it within about 0.4 m of SWOOP 2025 (EPSG:2958). Use the coordinates as they are; do not apply a NAD83-to-CSRS shift.

**Open fallback, and the default for anything shipped in textures: SWOOP 2025**
- Service: LIO GEO_Imagery_Data_Service_2023to2027 ImageServer.
- 16 cm, RGBN, captured March 13 - May 10 and November 24, 2025, leaf-off. Native EPSG:2958.
- Raster IDs: 66560, 66561, 66786, 66787, 67012, 67013.
- Licence: OGL-Ontario, so textures can be shipped with attribution.
- A second open option covering the whole course is the City of Waterloo 2021 10 cm MrSID (https://maps.waterloo.ca/OpenData/Waterloo_Aerial_Imagery_2021.zip, 3.9 GB). Its extent, 529000-544001 E by 4808000-4821001 N, contains the course. It is under the City of Waterloo Open Data Licence; I could not retrieve the full text, so confirm the commercial and attribution terms before shipping.
- Skip Esri World Imagery: its licence (the Esri MLA) forbids offline export.

**What the researchers missed**
1. The Ontario imagery-derived DSM from SWOOP 2020 (0.5 m, OGL-Ontario). It is useful for spotting changes since 2018.
2. The City of Waterloo 2023 7 cm summer layer (MapServer layer 8). It covers only the NW, Waterloo-side half of the course and is not open.
3. The City of Waterloo 2021 open SID, which covers the whole course.

**Corrections to the researchers' claims**
- An HRDEM STAC search at the course bbox returns 2 items, not 3. The third item (UTGR 2025) only appears in the wider 5 km search.
- The HRDEM DSM range read, which the researchers left untested, now works.
